The dismemberment of the Union, and the hostilities which might ensure, the abolition of Republican

No power upon earth can close upon the emigrants that fertile wilderness which offers resources
to all industry, and a refuge from all want.
Future events, of whatever nature they may be, will not deprive the Americans of their
climate or of their inland seas, of their great rivers, or of their exuberant soil.
Nor will bad laws, revolutions, and anarchy be able to obliterate that love of prosperity
and that spirit of enterprise which seem to be the distinctive characteristics of their
race, or to extinguish that knowledge which guides them on their way.
